the induced electric fields in different foetal tissues are significantly affected by the variation of conductivity values of the tissues; however the induced electric fields are always below the ICNIRPs basic restrictions.

the conductivity data of foetal tissues have a limited influence on the estimation of exposure to ELF-MF at 50 Hz.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the uncertainty in the estimation of the electric field induced by ELF-MFs at 50 Hz in the foetus is mainly due to the uncertainty in the conductivity of foetal tissues.

the uncertainty in the conductivity of foetal tissues does not significantly affect the induced electric fields in the foetal brain, but it may significantly affect the induced fields in foetal tissues such as fat.
, the influence of tissue conductivity in the estimation of the electric field induced during ELF-MF exposure to the foetus is not relevant in terms of compliance with the basic restriction levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the conductivity values for the tissues of the foetal body is critical in the estimation of the exposure to ELF-MFs.
, in order to obtain reliable exposure estimates for the foetus, a more accurate description of the conductivity of foetal tissues is needed.
the choice of the tissue conductivity values for the foetus is a crucial step in the dosimetry process, especially when the induced electric field is estimated using stochastic approaches.
